items.raw_snippet: ## How AI is Rewriting the Economics of Company-creation. This research brief explores why AI is compressing innovation cycles, how venture studios such as Nobody Studios are adapting to this new reality by creating innovation factories, and why enterprise leaders should rethink how innovation will be sourced during the next decade. This brief makes the case that it may be time to stop chasing unicorns as the new innovation playbook is acquisition, not build it all yourself. AI is changing not just how products are built, but the economics of innovation itself. * **AI is compressing the economics of company creation:** Agentic AI, cloud infrastructure, and reusable software have dramatically reduced the cost, talent, and time required to launch software businesses. * **The startup end game is changing:** Rather than pursuing long journeys toward IPOs, many AI-native companies are intentionally building highly differentiated capabilities designed for strategic acquisition. * **Venture studios are becoming the innovation factories of the AI era:** they discover opportunities, validate markets, and launch companies through a repeatable company-creation engine.

items.snippet: ## The Financial Brand. # Why M&A Is Less and Less about Assets, More and More a...
items.raw_snippet: ## The Financial Brand. # Why M&A Is Less and Less about Assets, More and More about Capabilities. Stay on top of all the latest news and trends in the banking industry. Mergers and acquisitions (M&A) in U.S. banking have moved from periodic consolidation to a structural strategy for survival and growth. According to a new SRM Perspectives report, financial institutions are using M&A to solve a shared set of constraints: rising technology costs, regulatory complexity, margin compression, and customer expectations shaped by digital-first competitors. Recent deal activity shows a clear shift toward larger, faster, and more strategic transactions, often involving strong institutions combining to achieve capabilities neither could build quickly on their own. The modern U.S. banking model is being reshaped by a simple constraint: fixed costs are rising faster than many institutions can scale revenue. As a result, scale has shifted from a strategic advantage to an operational requirement.

items.raw_snippet: # Pricing Agentic AI: A Practical Guide for Finance and Product Leaders. In this guide, we explain how to price agentic AI by moving beyond traditional per-seat licensing toward pricing models that align with AI-driven value and variable inference costs. The guide explores Per Agent, Per Activity, Per Output, Per Outcome, and hybrid pricing models, while introducing the COMPASS Framework and the Impossible Triangle to help finance and product leaders design scalable, profitable AI monetization strategies. **Agentic AI pricing is the discipline of charging for AI systems that take action autonomously, i.e.,  agents that don’t just answer questions but resolve tickets, close loops, generate artifacts, or complete workflows without human intervention at each step.** Pricing has to track the unit of value the agent delivers (an action, an output, or a business outcome) and the variable inference cost the agent consumes to deliver it.

items.raw_snippet: George Arison, the gay dating app’s chief executive, is aiming for all code to be eventually written by artificial intelligence, making the company “leaner.”. Grindr, the dating app used mostly by gay and bisexual men, bills itself as “the global gayborhood in your pocket.” When the service started, in 2009, it was novel to use smartphone geolocation to identify people near you. In 2022, Grindr hired George Arison as chief executive, to help the company go public that year. Mr. Arison, a longtime Silicon Valley entrepreneur who co-founded the ride-hailing app Curb and the used-car site Shift, was an early adopter of Grindr. In fact, he switched from a BlackBerry to an iPhone in 2009 in order to be able to use the app. The company aims for artificial intelligence to eventually produce all of its new code, and Mr. Arison says the company will become “leaner as time goes by.”.
